messages:
maya: FYI — Planned cold-start pressure test + rolling routing config change this Sunday 2026-03-29 02:00–04:00 UTC. Goal: exercise cold-start latency, KV cache warmup, and validate our automatic fallback to model-variants. Expect brief tail-latency spikes and a small uptick in 502s during pod drains. We'll throttle external traffic to Dedicated pool A and route overflow to fallback pool. Please read runbook and ack if you can be oncall or available.

tom: ack — I'll be oncall for the window, monitoring dashboards and RCs.

liam: what's the exact rollback trigger? CPU spike + error rate?

maya: primary rollback triggers: 
- sustained p50_latency > 200ms for >5m AND p99 > 2s
- 502 rate > 1% for 3m
- error budget burn rate > 2x baseline for 10m
If any trigger hits, we'll execute automatic fallback (route to model-variant v1.2-quantized) and then manual cutoff if needed. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/coldstart-pressure-test

ana: tagging infra — will we disable autoscaler for Dedicated pool A during the test?

maya: yes — autoscale will be pinned to baseline to force cold starts, but burst quota remains for emergency ops. We'll annotate the console so alerting doesn't flip to paged on expected blips.

sre-oncall: remind: please mute non-critical alerts and use the test label. Example Alert rule change: `severity:warning -> test` during 02:00-04:00 UTC.

tom: logging checklist: 
- enable full kvcache debug for affected nodes
- sample 1% of requests for full traces
Commands: 
```bash
kubectl label nodes dedicated-a test-window=true
kubectl annotate svc routing-policy rollback-contact=oncall
```

liam: who has keys for manual rollback?

maya: ana and tom have manual rollback perms; ops-runbook svc account can trigger fallback via `POST /ops/rollbacks` with X-Rollback-Auth.

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance: cold-start-pressure-test (window: 2026-03-29T02:00:00Z - 2026-03-29T04:00:00Z) — initiated by maya. See /maintenance/1805009876

ana: I'll be standing by on the #incident-call channel, can help with quick reconfigs.

tom: quick note — we'll run the ramp in 3 phases: 10% load, 40% load, 100% load. Pause and validate SLOs between phases.

maya: exactly. Phase timings: 02:00–02:20 (10%), 02:20–02:50 (40%), 02:50–03:50 (100%), 03:50–04:00 cool-down.

liam: adding a canary check: before 100% we run a canary against a different AZ for 15m. If anomalies, we stop and investigate.

ana: noted. I'll pre-warm the prometheus queries and dashboard panels so graphs don't throb on first load.

tom: please post back a short postmortem summary in #eng-sre after the window (one-pager: goals, what happened, metrics, actions).

maya: will do. Also scheduling a short async exec note for Product/Support with expected customer-facing impact: minimal, possible transient rate-limited requests.

sre-oncall: small reminder: set incident playbook state -> TESTING during window to suppress auto-runbook escalation.

liam: acked.

maya: thanks all. If you can't make it, say so now. Otherwise we'll proceed with the plan and I'll post live updates in this thread during the run. :eyes:
